title: About
text: Wooden Man Weather is a Marquette-focused weather dashboard and Monday work-week briefing. The dashboard shows National Weather Service forecasts, active alerts, and rolling twelve-month comparisons of temperature, precipitation, and snowfall against NOAA 1991–2020 normals for station USW00094850.

title: About
text:
How it updates
The site is built with Quarto and published to GitHub Pages. A GitHub Actions workflow renders the project on pushes to main and on a daily schedule so forecasts and climate caches stay current without a Shiny server.

title: About
text:
Attribution
Forecast and alert data: National Weather Service. Historical observations and normals: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information. This is an independent project and is not endorsed by NOAA or the NWS.

text:
Wooden Man Weather publishes a practical outdoor outlook each week for Marquette. Forecasts come from the National Weather Service; climate context uses NOAA daily summaries for station USW00094850. title: Monday work-week briefing
text:
Wooden Man tasks
Outdoor first. Foul weather gets an indoor stretch. No traffic tips — this is Marquette.









Task
Guidance




Briefing cadence
This weekly briefing refreshes for Monday mornings. The outdoor ideas still work any day — check back at the start of the week for a fresh set.


Lakeshore stretch
Start soft outside: ten quiet minutes on the Presque Isle rocks, a Fit Strip loop with nowhere to be, or a hammock and blanket with a friend at Tourist Park. Stay out longer than you meant to.


Wind day
If the breeze is up, it is kite weather on the open grass at Presque Isle — or just lean into the lake wind on a shore path bench. No kite? Same wind works. Board people: watch the water near the lower harbor / Ore Dock even if you are not on one.


Longer outdoor hang
Picnic blanket, throw, thermos — Fit Strip with sit-stops, a slow Presque Isle wander (lighthouse side, then grass), or hammock round two at dusk. Pointless and nice still counts.


Midweek local night
Marquette’s small-stage / open-mic energy usually shows up midweek. Check the current week at marquettemusicscene.com before you go — or use it as ‘what’s humming’ while you stay in with tea and a window cracked.


Before lake-effect settles in
Use the soft fall windows: longer Presque Isle sits, kite if it is breezy, blanket + friend while the grass is still kind. Indoors backup: Peter White Library or Dead River when the first lasting cold rain shows up.
